name: Sbu Chats

replaces.name: The Cringe: Chat Wrapped
replaces.price_model: free download, subscription required for all detailed stats and reports

replaces.name: ChatRecap AI - Chat Analysis
replaces.price_model: free for WhatsApp only, $3.99-4.99/week, one analysis per 24h, server-side AI

reference_outside_app_store: WhatStat (Google Play, com.whatstats, L. Scialpi): feature list used as a checklist only. ADR-0003: the spec is grounded on the App Store apps above.
one_thing: Turns an exported chat into its numbers, on the phone, and closes on one figure: how many messages you and the other person have sent.

features.name: Import an exported chat
features.description: Receive a .zip (with or without media) or .txt from the share sheet or Files; iOS and Android export formats; streaming line by line, never the whole file in memory.
features.reason: Every original's entry point. CFBundleDocumentTypes + UTImportedTypeDeclarations for public.zip-archive and public.plain-text; fileImporter for Files.

features.name: Who are you
features.description: On first import, pick which sender is you; remembered across chats.
features.reason: The export doesn't say who the owner is; every 'you vs them' stat needs it.

features.name: Chat overview
features.description: Total messages as the one figure, then per sender: messages, words, media, who starts and who ends conversations, longest streak of consecutive days.
features.reason: The Cringe's paywalled dashboard: 'total message count for each person', 'complete statistical dashboard'.

features.name: Response time
features.description: Median and average reply time per sender, from sender changes, capped at 24 h so overnight gaps don't skew it.
features.reason: Headline paid stat in The Cringe and ChatScope ('who replies faster').

features.name: Activity charts
features.description: Messages by hour, weekday, month and year, split by sender, with touch selection.
features.reason: Swift Charts, one GROUP BY strftime query per axis.

features.name: Top words and emoji
features.description: Most used words (stopwords removed, IT/EN/DE/ES/FR/PT) and emoji per sender, emoji counted per grapheme cluster (ZWJ, skin tones).
features.reason: The Cringe 'word frequencies', Luvlog 'most used words, emojis'. NLTokenizer + Character.unicodeScalars properties.

features.name: Date range filter
features.description: All, 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, custom range; applies to every stat.
features.reason: Needed to read any trend; DatePicker.

features.name: Every stat free, no daily limit
features.description: No 'locked' cards, no 24 h cooldown between analyses, unlimited chats.
features.reason: 21 of 45 reviews: everything paid, weekly price, one analysis per 24 h, stats shown as 'locked'.

features.name: Import that tells you why it failed
features.description: Parser tolerant to locales (dd/mm vs mm/dd detected from values > 12, 12/24 h, U+200E and U+202F), localized 'media omitted' strings in 8 languages; when a file isn't read, a plain error naming the line format found, never an endless spinner.
features.reason: 17 of 45 reviews: upload freezes, 'error', 'only found a few messages' on Spanish chats.

features.name: Truncation notice
features.description: Onboarding and the overview say WhatsApp exports at most about 40,000 messages without media and 10,000 with media, the most recent ones; the overview shows the first date found.
features.reason: Honest numbers: the 'reliability of figures' doubt (2 reviews) and the export limit.

features.name: Re-import and merge
features.description: Importing a newer export of the same chat merges it: key = chat name + hash of overlapping lines; duplicates dropped.
features.reason: Only way to build history past the export limit.

features.name: Word search
features.description: Search every message, exact phrase, AND/OR, filter by sender; shows who said it and when.

features.name: Milestone forecast
features.description: When the chat reaches 10k/50k/100k or a custom count, at the pace of the last 30 or 90 days.

features.name: Media gallery
features.description: Photos and videos from a with-media export, grid by date, QuickLook viewer; text-only import by default, media on request, delete media per chat; media excluded from backup.
features.reason: WhatStat feature; zips reach GB, so off by default.

features.name: Share card
features.description: One stat rendered as a 1080x1920 PNG with ImageRenderer and shared with ShareLink.
features.reason: 'Wrapped' is The Cringe's hook; no third-party URL schemes.

features.name: Monthly reminder to re-export
features.description: Optional local notification, off by default.
features.reason: Replaces WhatStat's live Root Mode, impossible on iOS.

screens.name: Chats
screens.purpose: List of imported chats (List .insetGrouped), import button, empty state explaining how to export from the messaging app.
elements: chat rows: name, messages, date range

screens.name: Chat
screens.purpose: The tool screen on surface: one figure (total messages, SbuStat + SbuFullStop), range filter, then per-sender sections.
elements: you vs them: messages, words, media, starts, ends

screens.name: Activity
screens.purpose: Charts by hour, weekday, month, year.

screens.name: Words
screens.purpose: Top words and emoji per sender, and search.

screens.name: Who are you
screens.purpose: First-import sheet to pick the owner among senders.

screens.name: Import error
screens.purpose: Explains a file that couldn't be read.
elements: mailto with the first line, only if the user chooses

flows.name: First import
steps: In the messaging app: chat > Export chat > without media

flows.name: Update a chat
steps: App recognises the chat and merges
Overview says how many new messages were added

data_model.storage: System SQLite (libsqlite3, FTS5 included) in Application Support, not SwiftData: 40k+ rows per chat and full-text search. Wrapped in a small type with Swift Testing tests. No iCloud: chats contain other people's personal data.

monetization.price: The Cringe: subscription for all detailed stats; ChatRecap AI $3.99-4.99/week, one analysis per 24 h
paywalled_features: more than one analysis per day (ChatRecap)
monetization.notes: ChatRecap uploads chats for server AI analysis; The Cringe and ChatScope claim on-device processing.

pains.pain: Everything paid: subscription for any detail, weekly price, one analysis per 24 h, stats shown as 'locked', no trial
pains.evidence: "$3.99 a week to only be able to use it once a day."
pains.becomes: Every stat free, no daily limit

pains.pain: Import or analysis fails: upload freezes, endless loading, error on files, few messages found on non-English chats
pains.evidence: "Solo se encontraron unos pocos mensajes. Verifica que exportaste"
pains.becomes: Import that tells you why it failed

pains.pain: Only works with WhatsApp; wants iMessage, Instagram
pains.evidence: "the fact that the only free option is whatsapp is CRAZY"
pains.becomes: skip: iMessage has no export on iOS; Instagram data download is a different, changing format (P2 later, not v1)

pains.pain: Doesn't tell senders apart or figures not trustworthy
pains.evidence: "non so quanto siano affidabili le cifre"
"This is a scam, it steals ur information"
pains.becomes: No network at all; stated in onboarding and Settings promises

pains_note: 45 reviews from The Cringe, ChatScope, ChatRecap AI and RealTalk (research/chats/reviews.json), counted by hand. Luvlog's 14 reviews are excluded: it is an 'online status tracker' that needs a server, a different and riskier niche.

skipped.feature: Live reading of the messaging app's database (WhatStat Root Mode)
skipped.reason: Impossible on iOS: no app can read another app's container.
Server-side in ChatRecap and RealTalk; on-device Foundation Models could do it but it judges third parties from their private messages: out of the one thing and a 5.1.2 risk.
Needs a server and the other person's account: surveillance, not stats.
Gamification outside the design system; the streak stays as a number.
ShareLink covers it without a third-party URL scheme.

system_frameworks.name: Compression (raw DEFLATE)
system_frameworks.use: unzip: own reader of the ZIP central directory (stored + deflate), streamed; no third-party unzip library

system_frameworks.name: NaturalLanguage
system_frameworks.use: NLTokenizer for words, language detection for stopwords

dependencies_note: The feasibility note proposed GRDB.swift and ZIPFoundation (both MIT). CLAUDE.md allows apps to depend only on SbuKit and Apple frameworks, so both are replaced: system sqlite3 and a ZIP reader on the Compression framework (about 150 lines, tested on real exports).

review_risks.risk: New Sbu app while six are in the Resolution Center; 'chat wrapped' apps are a small but growing niche.
review_risks.mitigation: Submit only after Apple answers the 14/10 lot, one per week; review notes: the only Sbu app that reads files from another app's export, no overlap with the others.

review_risks.risk: Using 'WhatsApp' in name, subtitle, icon or keywords.
review_risks.mitigation: Never in name, subtitle, keywords or screenshots. docs/factory.md forbids third-party app names in Store metadata: the description says 'chat esportate (.txt o .zip)'; the WhatsApp how-to lives on sbu.dev and in the in-app help, with 'WhatsApp è un marchio di Meta Platforms, Inc.; Sbu non è affiliata'.

review_risks.risk: Exports contain other people's personal data.
review_risks.mitigation: Nothing leaves the device, no iCloud, Privacy label 'Data Not Collected', delete per chat; review notes say so. No AI judgement of third parties.

review_risks.risk: Reviewer has no chat to export.
review_risks.mitigation: Bundled sample chat (written by us) behind 'Prova con una chat di esempio', and a screen recording in the notes.

review_risks.risk: Any attempt to read another app's data.
review_risks.mitigation: Only files the user shares or picks.
Sbu design system, one figure on surface, own copy and icon.

decisions_needed: Target iOS 17 (ADR-0002), not iOS 26 as in the feasibility note.
No full-field coloured dashboard: every screen sits on surface (CLAUDE.md).
Store description without the word WhatsApp, or an exception to the factory rule.
estimate_note: 12-15 days for 1.0; a first release with import, overview, response time, charts, words, filter and merge is about 8 days.

source.listing: research/chats/listing.json (5 App Store apps, US and IT)
